raw_response:
I'm 63 this year. I've farmed these 12.4 mu for forty years — since I was a young bride carrying water on a shoulder pole. Never went to school, can't read the fertilizer bags, but I know this soil better than any book. My husband is 65 and he goes off to construction work in the county town when they call him. It's mostly me and the land now, though he comes back for the wheat harvest in June.

I keep 8 mu for wheat-then-maize, and 4.4 mu on the south side for cotton. I've done it this way for twenty years. Cotton brings better money when the price is good, but it breaks your back with all the picking. Wheat-maize is safer — even if one crop suffers, the other usually feeds us.

The wheat is already in the ground since last October. Before planting, I spread one bag of compound fertilizer for every two mu — that's my rule, same as my mother-in-law did. In March when the wheat greened up, I walked the field with half a bag of urea per mu. The wheat looks alright this year, not as good as the year before last, but better than last year when the spring was too dry. I'll irrigate it once more when the heads come out, if the rain doesn't come first. Should get about eight hundred jin per mu.

For cotton, I'm planting this week around April 25th. The soil is warm enough. I plowed that field by hand last month when my nephew brought his ox. I'll put down one bag of compound for every two mu as base fertilizer. I saved some cotton seed but I bought two bags of new hybrid seed too — old seed sprouts weak. Cotton needs spraying for bugs, I use whatever the shop has, usually three times. I'll irrigate twice if it's dry. Picking is what kills me. I can handle the early bolls, but come September I hire two women from the east village for the main picking. Costs me eighty yuan per day each, but I can't bend down that many times anymore. If the worms stay away, maybe four to five hundred jin of lint per mu.

For maize, that comes after the wheat comes off in early June. No rest — the wheat is cut, and within two or three days the maize must go in or the season is lost. I hire Old Zhang's tractor to plant — thirty yuan per mu, but it saves my life. I put fertilizer in the furrow when we plant, half a bag of compound per mu and a small handful of urea. If the summer rains are good, I only irrigate once at the big growth stage. Last year I got nine hundred jin per mu, I'll be happy with the same.

Money is tight this year. Fertilizer prices went up again. I'm putting a little less on the cotton than I used to — maybe one less scoop per mu — because I need to keep cash aside for my husband's blood pressure medicine. But I won't cut the wheat fertilizer. Better to waste a bit of money than lose the crop. A bad year hurts more than a good year helps. That's what forty years taught me.

All in all, seed, fertilizer, water, hired tractor, and the picking women will cost me around five thousand yuan this year. That's a lot for two old people, but we have to live.
